transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-21
Start time: 16:00 PT
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Meyer (AE), Aisha Patel (SE), Noah Kim (SE), Marta Lopez (Head of Search), Devon Tran (Staff ML Eng), Priya Shah (Security Lead), Liam O'Connor (PM)
Shared artifacts: Deck: https://redwood.ai/decks/relevance-pinecrest (shared), Pilot template spreadsheet (link sent in chat)

[00:00] Jordan: All right, good afternoon everyone, thanks for taking the time. I'm Jordan from Redwood Inference, with Aisha and Noah on the call. How's everyone doing?
[00:07] Marta: Doing well, thanks. Excited to see the hosted flow — we've been evaluating several options for our search reranker.
[00:13] Devon: Hi all, the main thing for us is latency on mobile and regulatory constraints — we operate in EU and US, need data residency guarantees.
[00:20] Jordan: Great, that's exactly what we want to cover: the embeddings endpoint, the rerank endpoint, how the Console surfaces cost and latency, and the security controls for hosted deployments. Quick intro, Aisha — why don't you give a bit of context on what you'll demo?
[00:33] Aisha: Sure. I'll start with a short live API demo: generate embeddings for a small corpus, run a vector search, then call the reranker endpoint to re-score top-k results. I'll also open the Console to show per-route token cost, latency percentiles, and how you can pin model versions. I'll note some optimization knobs — batching settings and prefix caching — that reduce tokens and costs.
[00:52] Liam: One Q up front: our current pipeline uses Faiss for retrieval and a lightweight transformer for reranking. We're trying to reduce latency spikes while keeping precision. How does Redwood fit?
[01:03] Aisha: Good question. On hosted Redwood API, you can use embeddings for retrieval (we provide dimension-matched vectors for a number of open models), then call the dedicated reranker endpoint which is optimized for low-latency scoring — it uses a continuous batching runtime and KV cache for prefixes so repeated context doesn't re-tokenize. Typical top-k reranks for length ~256 context we see p50 latencies in the 60-120ms range depending on model/seq length and batching.
[01:28] Devon: 60-120ms p50 — is that warm or cold? Our SLA target is p95 < 300ms on mobile.
[01:36] Aisha: Those numbers are representative of warm-serving in hosted. Cold starts can be higher for model scale-ups, but you can configure reserved concurrency with Redwood Dedicated or reserved slots in hosted to lower variance. For pure hosted pilot we can configure reserved lanes to keep p95 within your target; we'll show Console metrics for that.
[01:55] Priya: From security perspective we need SOC2, SSO/SAML for our admins, and encryption keys under our control ideally. How do you handle KMS and audit logs?
[02:05] Jordan: We support customer-managed KMS in our Private deployments and for hosted we provide HSM-backed encryption; we also integrate with common KMS providers — we'll send the spec in the pack. Audit logs and per-token tracing are available via the Console and log export. For SSO we support SAML/SCIM and RBAC at workspace and route levels. We'll include the SOC2 and ISO artifacts in the follow-up.
[02:26] Priya: Okay, please send those. We also need clarity on data retention — can we disable retention of raw input after inference?
[02:33] Noah: Yes, for hosted pilots we can configure zero-retention mode for request payloads and only keep aggregated telemetry. If you later migrate to Private or VPC, you get full customer-managed controls.
[02:43] Marta: Cool. Can we see the actual API path and a quick demo?
[02:48] Aisha: Absolutely — I'll share my screen.
[02:51] [03:00] Aisha (screen): Okay so here's a sample notebook. First step: call POST /v1/embeddings with the text and model param. We're using a 1k-document sample for this demo. The response returns vector arrays — note the dimensions and a vector ID. I'll push those vectors to your vector DB — we're using Milvus in this demo but you can keep it in any index.
[03:23] Jordan: Quick aside, you can also use our managed embeddings index as an optional service if you want to avoid maintaining Milvus.
[03:29] Marta: You have a managed index? That could simplify a pilot. Any costs/limits?
[03:33] Jordan: Managed index is an add-on billed by storage and query units; we'll include details in pricing. For pilot it's easy to provision.
[03:40] [03:45] Aisha (screen): Next I'll run a vector query — top 50 candidates — then hit the reranker endpoint with the query + candidate documents. The reranker API accepts a list of candidate IDs plus the full context, and returns reranked IDs with scores and explainability tokens if configured. Watch the round-trip.
[04:05] [04:14] Aisha (typing): Sending request... got response. Top result changed after rerank — scoring bumped a medical guideline doc above a blog post, which is what you'd want for Pinecrest.
[04:24] Devon: Nice, how do you compute the rerank score? Is it cross-encoder style?
[04:28] Aisha: It's a cross-encoder reranker where the model ingests query+doc pairs, we do efficient batching on the backend. The score is a softmax-like logit converted to a 0-1 relevance. You can tune score thresholds and the reranker returns token-level attributions when you enable explainability, which helps investigate model drift.
[04:46] Liam: When you say explainability, is that deterministic? We need consistent signals for QA.
[04:52] Noah: The token attributions are model-derived saliency approximations — helpful signals but not a formal proof. However, we also surface model-level confidence and calibration metrics over your holdout prompts in Console so you can track drift and regressions.
[05:07] Marta: That calibration dashboard is important — we'll need it for product signoff.
[05:10] Aisha: We'll show that. Moving to Console — here's the per-route dashboard. It breaks down p50/p95 latency, per-request token counts, and cost per route. You can filter by model version and timeframe. I'll enable an overlay showing cache hit-rate; see this spike when prefix caching reduced tokens by ~40%.
[05:32] [05:41] Jordan: Quick note on batching: for rerank you can choose max_batch_latency (ms) and batch_size knobs. Lower latency targets reduce batching efficiency and raise per-request cost. We can recommend knobs based on your qps distribution.
[05:55] Devon: On qps: our peak query rate is roughly 350 qps across regions, with heavy tail during morning syncs. How does Redwood route across regions and maintain cost efficiency?
[06:06] Aisha: Smart routing can route requests by region or cost tier. For globally-distributed loads we recommend using regional endpoints with automatic fallback to backup regions. For cost, you can set routing policies to prefer lower-cost model variants or slightly quantized variants for non-critical routes.
[06:23] Priya: Does hosted support data residency? Some EU user data must stay in EU.
[06:27] Jordan: Yes — hosted supports region-specific endpoints and regional isolation. For strict residency you can opt for a Private deployment inside your VPC. For the pilot we can pin the EU requests to our eu-central region. We'll include the region map in the security pack.
[06:41] Marta: We also run periodic A/Bs between our current transformer and what we'd use as a reranker. Does Redwood have rollout tools?
[06:48] Aisha: Yes — in Console we have rollout controls: canary, A/B, and weighted routes with automatic fallback policies. You can pin users to a variant and roll out gradually; revert is one click. We can also tie rollout metrics to eval prompt sets so you get automatic regression alerts.
[07:04] Liam: Speaking of evals — can we upload our evaluation prompts to Console and get regression alerts?
[07:09] Noah: Yep. Console supports an eval suite where you upload prompt sets and golden labels; we run periodic checks and emit alerts when quality drops beyond thresholds. This is how you catch model drift after a model update.
[07:20] Marta: We're interested in embeddings model selection — what models do you recommend for clinical note search?
[07:26] Aisha: For clinical text, models trained on medical corpora or open models fine-tuned for biomedical are preferred. We host a catalog with verified embeddings models and provide performance profiles per domain (recall at k, cosine stability). For initial pilot use a smaller embedding (512 dim) to reduce compute and storage; if semantic nuance requires bigger vectors we can upgrade.
[07:45] Devon: Any built-in deduping or duplicate detection on ingestion? We have a lot of near-duplicate notes.
[07:50] Aisha: We provide an ingestion pipeline pattern that includes shingled hashing and clustering; not a managed dedupe product for now but we'll share the pattern and code snippets.
[07:59] [08:05] Priya: Let's return to compliance: Priya here. For hosted pilot, what control do we get over encryption keys and logs? Can we enforce customer-managed KMS?
[08:14] Jordan: For hosted pilots, full customer-managed KMS is supported for workspace-level secrets in Private deployments; for hosted we have HSM-backed keys and can integrate with your KMS through a key-wrapping approach. We'll include the exact architecture diagram in the follow-up. Audit logs are exportable to your SIEM via secure forwarder.
[08:33] Priya: Good — also need contractual language about data deletion windows and penalties.
[08:38] Jordan: We'll involve legal after this call; we'll send the relevant SLO and data processing addenda.
[08:44] [08:50] Aisha: Back on the demo — I'll show an example of cost optimization. We ran a pilot where switching from a 1536-dim embedding to a 512-dim with reranker saved 60% on embedding storage and reduced average query cost by 30% while keeping MRR within 1.5% of baseline. These are the kinds of tradeoffs we can recommend per workload.
[09:10] Liam: That's promising. What's the instrumentation needed on our side to measure MRR and latency for rollouts?
[09:16] Aisha: Minimal. You send request IDs and ground-truth labels to the eval suite or export logs back to your analytics pipeline. We can ingest metrics from your telemetry endpoint too.
[09:26] Devon: For the reranker call shape: how many docs can we send in one request? We normally take top 200 and rerank top 20.
[09:33] Aisha: Reranker accepts up to 512 candidates depending on model length, but we recommend pre-filtering to the top 100 and reranking top 20-50 for latency tradeoffs. You can also stream partial results if you want early responses.
[09:47] Marta: Streaming partial results — how consistent are ranked results if stream returns? Could be confusing for UI.
[09:52] Noah: Streaming is best for long documents or when you want the first plausible result quickly; final ranking is provided when the full rerank completes. For UI we'll usually show a stable top-3 and then refine.
[10:04] [10:12] Jordan: Let's talk pilot scope. Typical pilot: 2 weeks hosted, ingest a 10k-50k doc subset, run evals on 1-2k held-out queries, and provide a recommendations report. We'll include suggested success criteria like p95 < 300ms, MRR delta <= 2% from baseline, and cost per query under $X.
[10:34] Liam: Timeline works. We have a legal review window of ~3 weeks, security needs the SOC2 docs asap.
[10:40] Jordan: We'll get the SOC2 pack to Priya today.
[10:43] Priya: Thanks. Also can we run a short penetration test?
[10:47] Jordan: Yes, we allow customer pen tests per the process in the security pack; we'll include the request form.
[10:54] Devon: One more technical — how do you prevent token explosion when reranking many candidates? Our docs can be long.
[10:59] Aisha: We support document chunking and use a context window sliding approach plus a candidate selection policy. For long docs we score by highest-relevance chunk, and you can store precomputed chunk embeddings so the reranker only receives the top chunks not the full document. That keeps token counts manageable.
[11:17] Marta: That matches our approach.
[11:20] [11:25] Jordan: We're nearing the end; let's recap. Action items: Jordan will send pricing and security pack; Aisha will set up a trial rerank demo with your sample dataset; Devon will send the 10k manifest; Priya will list compliance questions. Any other asks?
[11:41] Liam: Can you include an itemized estimate of cost for 350 qps sustained with our traffic profile?
[11:46] Jordan: Yes — we'll prepare a tailored cost projection in the pricing sheet.
[11:49] Marta: And a note about model variants we should try first — maybe 512-dim embeddings + a medium reranker.
[11:56] Aisha: We'll recommend two embeddings and two reranker variants for the pilot.
[12:01] Priya: Please also include the retention controls and the regional isolation steps in writing.
[12:06] Jordan: Will do.
[12:09] [12:15] Marta: Thanks everyone, very helpful. Looking forward to the pilot.
[12:18] Jordan: Thanks — we'll follow up by EOD tomorrow with the docs and scheduling links.
[12:25] Devon: Thanks all.
[12:27] [12:30] Meeting end

Notes on transcript quality: auto transcription had a few mislabels (Noah sometimes labeled as Speaker 3), some technical acronyms transcribed with spaces (K V cache) and product names garbled in one line. The content above was lightly edited for readability but retains conversational turns, filler words, and occasional interruptions.
